transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park, Mateo Ruiz, Asha Kapoor, Derek Long (Redwood); Priya Nair, Owen Cheng, Sophie Lambert, Marcus Albright (VelaTide)
Recording ID: ffx-20260514-vela-0112

Summary:
Quick technical sync to align on marketplace listing connector for VelaTide's LLM Gateway, validate network/KMS constraints for Redwood Private/Dedicated options, and plan a hands-on connector lab. Primary concerns: egress latency, KMS integration for on-prem keys, and packaging for marketplace listing.

Topics covered:
- VelaTide architecture & constraints (on-prem transit boxes, split-control plane)
- Redwood connector packaging: Helm chart + binary sidecar options
- KMS/HSM and audit log requirements
- Performance baseline and fallback routing (hosted -> dedicated -> private)
- Next steps and scheduling of lab

Action items (as stated in call):
- See action_items above and next_steps (documented).

Transcript body:
00:00 - Speaker 1 (Lena Park): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check on audio?
00:08 - Speaker 2 (Priya Nair): Yep, can hear you. Thanks Lena. Appreciate the time, we wanted to make sure the connector path for the marketplace listing is viable for us.
00:15 - Speaker 1 (Lena Park): Great. I'll hand over to Mateo to run through the connector patterns we typically ship, then we can map to VelaTide's infra.
00:24 - Speaker 3 (Mateo Ruiz): Cool. So, at a high level we have two common delivery patterns: a Helm chart that deploys a Redwood connector as a sidecar to the LLM Gateway, and a binary/operator install for air-gapped/on-prem customers. The Helm path is faster for cloud marketplaces. Note: when I say "connector" I mean the agent that handles auth, routing, and optional local KV-cache — sometimes the notes say K-V cash which is actually KV cache, sorry.
00:47 - Speaker 4 (Owen Cheng): Quick q: is the sidecar going to hold any customer keys or is everything proxied to Redwood KMS? We need to keep key material on our HSM.
00:55 - Speaker 3 (Mateo Ruiz): Good question. We support two modes: mTLS proxy where all tokens are proxied and keys stay in your HSM, and a hybrid where a lightweight PKCS#11 shim talks to the HSM and only ephemeral signing data is exchanged. For marketplace listing, we typically demonstrate the mTLS proxy path — less friction.
01:18 - Speaker 2 (Priya Nair): If we do mTLS proxy, what about latency? Our gateway has tight SLA for token round-trip.
01:25 - Speaker 3 (Mateo Ruiz): Right. We instrumented typical one-way extra latency of 8-25ms depending on whether connector is colocated. If you colocate the sidecar in the same pod/node, it’s in the single-digit ms. If it's cross-az, it can spike. We can show perf numbers in the lab.
01:45 - Speaker 5 (Sophie Lambert): Also we need to validate audit trails — Redwood's audit log format, retention, and whether we can ship logs to our SIEM.
01:53 - Speaker 1 (Lena Park): Asha can cover audit and RBAC.
01:56 - Speaker 6 (Asha Kapoor): Sure — we export structured audit events (JSON lines) with token-level opcodes, model/version, and request metadata. Default retention on Hosted is 30 days but for Dedicated/Private we can configure retention and forward to customer S3/Syslog or send via forwarders to Splunk/Elastic. For marketplace listing, we include a sample forwarding config in the repo.
02:17 - Speaker 4 (Owen Cheng): When you say "model/version" sometimes your generated transcript earlier said Redwood-verified model profiles were mis-xyz — what's the exact field? We need stable identifiers for reproducible rollouts.
02:28 - Speaker 6 (Asha Kapoor): We use model_id and model_sha in headers — model_id is a stable catalog name, model_sha is the build fingerprint. We'll include the mapping doc.
02:35 - Speaker 7 (Marcus Albright): On the networking side, our infra blocks 443 outbound except for a small allowlist. We'll likely need to open some CIDRs or NAT endpoints. Can Redwood provide an allowlist?
02:45 - Speaker 3 (Mateo Ruiz): Yes, we'll provide a list; for Private deploys we can also use VPC peering. For Hosted we publish a short list of egress IP ranges, but note those can change during scale events, which is why many customers prefer VPC peering for predictability.
03:03 - Speaker 2 (Priya Nair): Another constraint — we run a transit box in the colo that performs TLS termination and a policy layer. Sidecar might not be allowed to talk directly outbound. Can the connector be fronted by a proxy?
03:14 - Speaker 3 (Mateo Ruiz): Absolutely — the connector can be configured to talk via your corporate proxy. We have docs for proxy env vars, and an HTTP CONNECT passthrough mode for websockets/streaming. Small caveat: streaming with an intermediary can add buffering latencies; we'll demonstrate that in the lab.
03:40 - Speaker 1 (Lena Park): Let's pivot to listing packaging. Derek, want to walk through demo artifact expectations?
03:45 - Speaker 8 (Derek Long): Yep. For marketplace we need: a reference architecture doc, a deployment artifact (Helm or operator), security checklist, and a quickstart that includes a sample app and perf notes. We'll also want a canned test that demonstrates fallback: hosted -> dedicated -> private with metrics.
04:05 - Speaker 4 (Owen Cheng): Fallbacks sound good, how is routing decided? Weighted? Latency? Cost?
04:11 - Speaker 8 (Derek Long): Smart routing is policy driven. We can show examples: latency-first, cost-first, and region-first. For your use-case with strict latency, we'd recommend latency-first with a canary path to dedicated for heavy flows.
04:25 - Speaker 5 (Sophie Lambert): Security review: do you support SAML SSO for admin console access and SCIM provisioning? Also RBAC mapping to our existing groups?
04:34 - Speaker 6 (Asha Kapoor): Yes to SAML and SCIM for the console. For the connector, we map service accounts to roles via a simple YAML mapping. We'll send a mapping template.
04:45 - Speaker 7 (Marcus Albright): Perf: what baseline tokens/sec for a single small GPU in dedicated mode? We need numbers to plan capacity.
04:54 - Speaker 3 (Mateo Ruiz): Typical small 80GB A10-style GPU baseline for 8k context can do ~30-40 streaming tokens/sec depending on quant, batching. For smaller contexts and quantized weights it's higher. We'll bring a perf spreadsheet. Note: these numbers are approximate, real numbers vary with prompt distribution.
05:20 - Speaker 2 (Priya Nair): Any compatibility issues with our in-house token cache layer? We keep a prefix cache on Redis; does Redwood caching interact?
05:29 - Speaker 3 (Mateo Ruiz): We support prefix/KV cache in two ways: internal cache in the connector for hot prefixes, or an integration hook to talk to your Redis via a small adapter. We'll show the Redis adapter in the repo.
05:47 - Speaker 4 (Owen Cheng): About the Helm chart — do you publish in a public chart repo for marketplace listings?
05:53 - Speaker 8 (Derek Long): For marketplace we provide a packaged chart (tarball) and a CI pipeline snippet to sign & publish. For private/air-gapped customers we provide an operator that can be installed from an image bundle.
06:08 - Speaker 5 (Sophie Lambert): For KMS, if we keep key material in our HSM, what's the attestation story? Does Redwood require key export for model signing?
06:16 - Speaker 3 (Mateo Ruiz): No key export required. Our PKCS#11 shim performs attestations using ephemeral public keys that Redwood verifies. We can do mutual TLS with client certs from your HSM-backed CA. We'll need to run a short compatibility test with your vendor (you mentioned Thales earlier?).
06:33 - Speaker 5 (Sophie Lambert): Yes. Thales Luna is what we have.
06:36 - Speaker 3 (Mateo Ruiz): Perfect — we'll add Thales notes.
06:40 - Speaker 2 (Priya Nair): Great. Can we talk about observability — do you emit per-request traces? We want to join with our existing tracing (Jaeger).
06:48 - Speaker 6 (Asha Kapoor): We emit OpenTelemetry spans and can push to OTLP endpoints. For marketplace, the default is to send to Redwood Trace, but customers can configure OTLP endpoint to forward traces to their Jaeger/Tempo. We'll include a sample OTLP config in the repo.
07:05 - Speaker 7 (Marcus Albright): Streaming edges — if we run the connector on premise and use your hosted models as a fallback, is streaming preserved end to end?
07:13 - Speaker 3 (Mateo Ruiz): Streaming can be preserved via chunked transfer or websockets. If proxying through your transit, websockets are preferred. Chunked transfer may be buffered by some proxies which introduces sawtooth latency. We'll demo both.
07:30 - Speaker 1 (Lena Park): Alright, let's move to the hands-on lab plan and timing. We're proposing a two hour lab with bench scripts: connectivity, KMS handshake, small perf run (1000 requests), and streaming correctness test.
07:44 - Speaker 2 (Priya Nair): That sounds good. Who should be in the lab from our side?
07:48 - Speaker 7 (Marcus Albright): Marcus + Sophie + Owen ideally. Marcus will run infra changes.
07:52 - Speaker 1 (Lena Park): Okay we'll schedule for week of 2026-05-25. Mateo, Derek, Asha will run the lab. We'll send calendar invite.
08:00 - Speaker 4 (Owen Cheng): Before the lab, can Mateo share a lightweight smoke test script we can run to validate networking?
08:06 - Speaker 3 (Mateo Ruiz): Yes, I'll push a curl-based smoke script to the repo. It will test TLS handshake, simple call, and streaming sample.
08:14 - Speaker 5 (Sophie Lambert): On compliance packaging — for our procurement we need a short summary doc: SOC2 scope, encryption-at-rest, key management, and data residency statement. Can Redwood provide?
08:22 - Speaker 1 (Lena Park): We'll share Redwood compliance pack and a short one-pager for procurement.
08:28 - Speaker 6 (Asha Kapoor): Also adding a note: for marketplace listing we include a preflight checklist that covers network, KMS, and auditing expectations — we'll attach it.
08:36 - Speaker 2 (Priya Nair): One more question on pricing: if we burst to Dedicated from Hosted during traffic spikes, how is billing handled?
08:45 - Speaker 8 (Derek Long): Billing for Dedicated is usually committed capacity; we can set up automatic fallback with burst credits from Hosted, and we'd show example pricing scenarios in the commercial handoff. For the pilot we'll use a credit-backed test.
08:56 - Speaker 7 (Marcus Albright): Minor but important — what ports need to be open from our transit box? 443 is default, but any outbound to uncommon ports for health checks?
09:05 - Speaker 3 (Mateo Ruiz): Mostly 443 outbound. Health checks call back to a Redwood endpoint on 443. For HSM PKCS#11 adapters you may have local sockets only.
09:15 - Speaker 2 (Priya Nair): Good. Ok, recap and next steps?
09:20 - Speaker 1 (Lena Park): Recap: Redwood shares connector repo, quickstart, audit forwarding examples; VelaTide shares network topology and Thales Luna contact; schedule lab week of 05/25; action items and due dates as noted.
09:34 - Speaker 4 (Owen Cheng): Thanks all, we'll try to get the topology doc to you by 05/21.
09:38 - Speaker 1 (Lena Park): Great thanks everyone. Invite to follow.
